_meta.indication: Treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults 18 years of age and older
_meta.receipt_date: 02/25/2011 (Received Date of the Standard-Resubmission / Complete Response reviewed under NDA 22-150)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to a single dose of icatibant 30 mg SC versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥ 18 years with Type I or Type II hereditary angioedema presenting with an acute attack
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: time from blinded treatment administration to onset of symptom relief, defined as a 50% reduction from pretreatment in the mean composite VAS score of three symptom domains (abdominal pain, skin pain, skin swelling)
pivotal_trials.n: 88 subjects randomized 1:1 to icatibant 30 mg SC versus placebo for the initial non-laryngeal HAE attack; non-laryngeal ITT population was 43 icatibant versus 45 placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to onset of symptom relief (composite VAS-3) was 2.0 hours with icatibant versus 19.8 hours with placebo (p < 0.001); 43 of 43 icatibant vs 42 of 45 placebo recipients achieved symptom relief

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of Icatibant in Patients With Acute Attacks of Hereditary Angioedema (FAST-3)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions, which occurred in almost all patients (97%); other reactions >1% of patients included pyrexia (4%), transaminase increased (4%), dizziness (3%), and rash
target_moa: Icatibant is a competitive antagonist selective for the bradykinin B2 receptor; in HAE, deficiency/dysfunction of C1-esterase-inhibitor leads to bradykinin overproduction causing swelling, and icatibant inhibits bradykinin from binding the B2 receptor

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary and Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met June 23, 2011; voted that efficacy data were sufficient (12 Yes, 1 No), that safety data were adequate (11 Yes, 1 No, 1 Abstain), and in favor of approval (12 Yes, 1 No)

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted for icatibant; HAE is categorized as an orphan disease in the US

citations.quote: The Agency and the applicant had various interactions dating back to 2003 when the applicant first came to the Agency seeking an orphan drug designation for icatibant, which was granted.
HAE is estimated to affect 1 in 10,000 to 50,000 individuals worldwide and is categorized as an orphan disease in the US.

summary.text: Icatibant is a new molecular entity (the first bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist) that received orphan drug designation for HAE. The original 505(b)(1) NDA received a Not Approvable action because the clinical data did not provide substantial evidence of efficacy; the sponsor submitted a Complete Response on February 25, 2011 adding the placebo-controlled FAST-3 trial. A PADAC meeting on June 23, 2011 voted in favor of approval (12 Yes, 1 No), and the NDA was approved.

citations.quote: Icatibant is a new molecular entity and is the first drug in its class of bradykinin type 2 receptor antagonists.
